newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares see lazy summer, longer term growth.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares see lazy summer, longer term growth.

text.p: Leading Russian shares, which have powered to six consecutive closing records, have not seen their growth limit this year but have begun to cool off for the summer, stock analysts said on Thursday.
"Prices are not going to remain at these levels," said CentreInvest Securities research chief James Fenkner, voicing widespread belief that short-term profit-taking had begun.

"The blue chips have been bid up to record levels so quickly...that I see a levelling off this week," said Sadie Wighton, senior analyst at Regent European Securities, adding July and August are traditionally quiet months.

Traders said profit taking had already started to chip into record gains late on Wednesday, and the Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at 432.86, slightly off Wednesday's record 433.12 close. Wednesday market volume was a record $94 million.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell research head for the CIS Jim Nail said some stocks could slip by as much as 15 percent, with easing spread over a couple of months in the worst case.
But many analysts said leading Russian stocks, especially those which underperformed earlier in the year, still had room to rise over the rest of the year on positive fundamentals.
"Russia is the best performing equity market in the world," said Nail. "Over the rest of year it will resume growth and I'm confident we will see new record levels," he added.

Leading shares blasted off last week after several months' lull and traders and analysts said an influx of new funds from abroad had surged into undervalued leading shares on approval of reforms engineered by a dynamic young cabinet.

Tough government positions on budget spending cuts, a key tax reform bill and forcing companies to settle tax debts were encouraging investors, traders said, as well as Russia's inclusion in the Paris Club of creditors.
Nail said he had seen the Moscow Times index, which rose to 320.67 on Wednesday, at 330 by the end of the year. Wighton said 10-20 percent growth by the end of the year was realistic.
"Most portfolios are underweighted in Russia," said Rinaco Plus trader Tom Brackenbury. "There is potential for further allocations."

"There are plenty of investment funds which have no interest in Russia yet," said Wighton, adding new investors would seek liquid shares. "The market is up over 100 percent already since January and that will tempt more conservative money."
Analysts said leading shares would be the conduit for many new funds from large investors this year.

Russia's biggest oil producer LUKoil LKOH.RTS accounts for about 13 percent of the market's capitalisation. Its highly liquid shares opened at $19.90 after a $21.00 close. The share price was $16.20 on June 12.
"I think that there is a flow of funds explanation for what is going on," Nail said. But he said fundamentally cheap Russian companies would see strong gains this year.
Fenkner said the market would broaden over the doldrums of summer. Fund flows may slow and investors may move some funds from leading shares to more undervalued second tier stocks.
The best results of the summer may not be on the RTS index, which tracks the 22 most liquid shares.

"I don't know if we'll see LUKoil at $25 this summer, but we will see a broadening of the market unless U.S. interest rates go up," he said. "Fundamentally Russia remains very cheap. Some of the blue chips are less cheap and that's why you're going to see a broadening of the market."
